question: A 27-year-old man presents to the emergency department after a dog bite. The patient was intoxicated and pulled the dog’s tail while it was eating. The dog belongs to his friend and is back at his friend’s house currently. Physical exam is notable for a dog bite on the patient’s right arm. The wound is irrigated and explored with no retained bodies found. A tetanus vaccination is administered. Which of the following is appropriate management of this patient?

options.opb: Administer the rabies vaccine and rabies immunoglobulin
options.opd: Close the wound with sutures and discharge the patient
options.ope: Discharge the patient with outpatient follow up

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Dog bite -> Risk of infection -> Tetanus vaccination administered -> 95% CHAIN: Dog bite -> High risk of rabies transmission -> Administer rabies vaccine and rabies immunoglobulin -> 90% CHAIN: Dog bite -> Common pathogens involved -> Administer amoxicillin-clavulanic acid -> 80% CHAIN: Dog bite -> Risk of infection -> Wound exploration with no retained bodies -> Close the wound with sutures -> 75% CHAIN: Dog bite -> Risk of infection -> Wound exploration with no retained bodies -> Discharge the patient with outpatient follow-up -> 95%
analysis: Given the circumstances of the dog bite and the lack of signs of infection or retained bodies in the wound, the appropriate management for this patient would be to administer the rabies vaccine and rabies immunoglobulin as a precautionary measure due to the nature of the dog's behavior and the patient's intoxicated state. Rabies is a serious and potentially fatal viral infection that can be transmitted through the saliva of infected animals, including dogs.
